1. Core Clinical Tension: An adolescent stem cell transplant recipient (18 months post-allogeneic transplant for acute myeloid leukemia, off immunosuppression) presenting with acute febrile illness and isolated thrombocytopenia. The core clinical challenge is differentiating an acute endemic viral infection from early leukemic relapse, graft dysfunction, or invasive opportunistic infection.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The presentation ends after initial triage evaluation reveals acute intermittent fever (24-48 hours) and isolated thrombocytopenia, immediately prior to arboviral antigen testing and inpatient supportive care.
3. Differential Distinctions: Differentiating acute arboviral infection from acute myeloid leukemia recurrence (ruled out by lack of marrow failure or blast proliferation), secondary graft failure, and bacterial sepsis (ruled out by an uncomplicated, self-limited clinical course).
case_prompt: A 16-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia, who had undergone a matched-sibling donor hematopoietic stem cell transplant 18 months earlier and was off all immunosuppressive therapy, presented with a 24- to 48-hour history of intermittent fever. Initial triage blood counts revealed isolated thrombocytopenia without other hematologic or organ abnormalities.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Acute Myeloid Leukemia Relapse / Secondary Graft Failure
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to post-allogeneic transplant status and new-onset cytopenia, but ruled out by isolated, transient thrombocytopenia without systemic progression or peripheral blasts.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: He only had thrombocytopenia, without any significant complications.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered in any post-transplant febrile episode, but ruled out by a benign clinical course resolving with simple supportive measures without broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: He was successfully managed as an in-patient with hydration, analgesics, antipyretics, and serial monitoring of blood counts for 5 days.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Rapid detection of viral antigen in a patient presenting with acute fever and isolated thrombocytopenia in an endemic region established the diagnosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: presented with intermittent fever for 24-48 h and found to be positive for dengue NS1 antigen.

editor_comments: Distilled admission teaching case for Dengue virus infection post-HSCT. Breakpoint strictly excludes NS1 result and inpatient course. Verbatim quotes validated.
